- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model often holds too high; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast with 5–10% downward correction starting from day of sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend (≥ 3% drop/day), model often overestimates early; reduce forecast by 2–4% per day for first 3–5 days.
